sentences.text: 2. Listen to the second part of Brunch with Charlie in which the host Charlie Meadows continues with his interview.
Listen and fill in the missing information in the spaces below.
You now have 30 seconds to study the task.
At the end of the task, you will have one minute to tidy up your answers.
Now, Dr Lee you wanted to make a special announcement.
Is that right?
Yes, that’s right.
As you said the committee has just been set up and we are looking for more people, more members of the general public to join the committee.
So I’m here to ask your listeners if they would be interested in getting involved in choosing a twin city for Hong Kong by coming on to the committee.
Can it be anyone?
Well there are going to be three groups of people on the committee: politicians, students, and a general public.
What were the exact numbers we are looking for, Lamy?
Um, Yes, we're looking for five students and five members of the general public.
Yeah, that’s right.
And we would be delighted if the listeners of your radio show applied.
Great. So what about students?
Is it open to primary school students?
No that’s a bit young, it’s open to secondary school students and university students.
So secondary school and university students, right?
That's right. So what about the members of the general public?
Any age limits?
Well for the general public group if you want to reply, you have to be retired.
Retired! Now that’s what I call an age limit!
it. Why so?
Well one reason is that they have more time than people who are working.
Ah, you mean more time to attend the meetings?
No, not really.
What I mean is time to do some research.
That sort of thing.
But more importantly, they have a lot of life experience to offer.
Oh, OK. So you senior citizens, if you're listening we want you.
OK, and what kind Well, we are looking for two qualities in all the applicants.
OK. We are looking for someone with knowledge of Hong Kong.
Ah I see, so they can share this knowledge of Hong Kong with the twin city, right?
Yes, and the second quality is they should have a real enthusiasm for other cultures.
Yeah, I can see that, yes.
I mean, we'd really want to have people on board who have that, you know, enthusiasm for cultures for other countries.
Great. Oh, I have another question.
Do people applying for the committee have to be from Hong Kong?
Actually no, They can be any nationality.
As long as they have been living in Hong Kong for at least three years.
That's fine. I see, so open to any nationality but must have been here for 3 years, Well it all sounds awesome to me.
So how do listeners apply for a place on the committee and what's the deadline?
Let me. do you have the details there?
Yeah, um, applications are open now and they should be submitted online.
The deadline is the 30th of June.
So online applications.
By the end of June.
Yes, that’s right.
Gotcha. Wait a minute.
You said politicians before.
What about the politicians on the committee?
Are you choosing them too?
Well, the politicians on the committee have already been chosen.
Already been chosen?
Why is that?
Well, we want to represent all the political parties in Hong Kong.
OK, I suppose that’s fair to try to represent all the political parties.
Absolutely. OK, so many thanks to you both.
And maybe we can have you back in the studio sometime in the future to tell our listeners which city was chosen.
chosen. Yes, that would be great.
